issues.description: The UML in the problem statement marks the Animal constructor as private ("- Animal(String): void"), which contradicts the intended design shown in the textual instructions and the solution. A private Animal(String) would prevent subclasses from calling super(...) and block creating concrete animal instances as demonstrated in Main and the solution. This inconsistency can confuse students about the correct visibility for the Animal constructor.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the UML and problem statement consistent with the intended implementation: change the Animal constructor visibility in the UML to protected or public (protected is recommended so subclasses can call super(name) but Animal cannot be instantiated directly). Alternatively, add an explicit note in the problem text that the Animal(String) constructor must be accessible to subclasses (protected/public).
